newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bolivar slumps as CenBank stays away.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bolivar slumps as CenBank stays away.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar slumped in heavy trade to 478.00/479.00 per dollar in an apparently deliberate move by the Central Bank to let the unit soften, traders said.
The fall "makes sense as the exchange rate has been anchored flat for some time now," said one trader.
"The Central Bank only sold gobbits of dollars in the morning, and then mostly let the exchange rate slide in the afternoon," he added.

The bolivar closed Monday at 477.50/478.50. The bolivar has depreciated less than three percent since exchange controls were removed almost exactly a year ago -- despite domestic inflation of over 70 percent.
